title: Deep Nuclei Atlas
subtitle: Explore thalamic, striatal, pallidal, subthalamic and claustral systems
altText: Chalkboard-style interactive anatomical illustration for Deep Nuclei Atlas, showing labelled structures and pathway relationships.
learningObjectives: Identify the major components of deep nuclei.
Trace clinically relevant inputs, outputs and connections.
Relate focal dysfunction to plausible neurological and behavioural signs.

sections.explainSimply: Deep Nuclei is a set of connected structures that can be explored layer by layer to understand where it sits and what it does.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: This atlas links the anatomy of deep nuclei to behaviour, cognition, neurological signs and clinically meaningful patterns without reducing complex functions to one structure.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: The deep nuclei should be interpreted through spatial relationships, laterality, vascular supply, pathway continuity and distributed network effects. Focal damage can create both local signs and disconnection syndromes.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of it as a layered transit map: structures are stations, tracts are routes, and symptoms depend on which junctions or connections are interrupted.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Recognising plausible neuroanatomical patterns supports better referral, formulation and interpretation of cognitive or behavioural change.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Over-localising a symptom to one structure, or treating an atlas view as diagnostic evidence, can produce false certainty.
sections.clinicalPearl: Its head, body and tail curve with the lateral ventricle.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician can select a structure in the Deep Nuclei Atlas and trace its inputs and outputs before comparing the predicted pattern with examination, imaging and functional assessment.
sections.limitationsCautions: This atlas supports learning and clinical reasoning; it does not replace neurological examination, imaging or specialist interpretation.

anatomy.label: Caudate nucleus
anatomy.function: Action selection, learning and cognitive loops
anatomy.connections: Cortex and substantia nigra; projects to Globus pallidus and substantia nigra.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Its head, body and tail curve with the lateral ventricle.

anatomy.label: Putamen
anatomy.connections: Motor and somatosensory cortex; projects to Globus pallidus and substantia nigra.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: The putamen is the lateral part of the dorsal striatum.

anatomy.label: Globus pallidus
anatomy.function: Major inhibitory output and relay of basal-ganglia loops
anatomy.connections: Striatum and subthalamic nucleus; projects to Thalamus and brainstem.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Internal and external segments have different roles in direct and indirect pathways.

anatomy.label: Subthalamic nucleus
anatomy.connections: Cortex and external pallidum; projects to Internal pallidum and substantia nigra.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: A small lesion can cause dramatic contralateral flinging movements.

anatomy.label: Substantia nigra
anatomy.connections: Striatum and subthalamic nucleus; projects to Striatum, thalamus and brainstem.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Pars compacta and pars reticulata serve distinct modulatory and output functions.

anatomy.label: Thalamic nuclei
anatomy.function: Relay and regulate sensory, motor and associative information
anatomy.inputs: Cortex, basal ganglia, cerebellum and sensory pathways
anatomy.connections: Cortex, basal ganglia, cerebellum and sensory pathways; projects to Cerebral cortex.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: The thalamus is a family of nuclei, not a single relay station.

anatomy.label: Claustrum
anatomy.function: Widespread cortical integration; function remains uncertain
anatomy.connections: Broad cortical input; projects to Broad cortical output.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Its extensive connectivity is established, but strong claims about consciousness remain speculative.

quiz.question: What is the safest way to use the Deep Nuclei Atlas?
options: As a spatial and network guide alongside clinical evidence
To assume one symptom has one location
quiz.rationale: As a spatial and network guide alongside clinical evidence

quiz.question: Which principle best improves lesion interpretation?
options: Consider location, pathways, laterality and network effects
Assume all people have identical anatomy
quiz.rationale: Consider location, pathways, laterality and network effects

quiz.question: What does selecting a structure reveal?
options: Function, inputs, outputs, connections and clinical relevance
quiz.rationale: Function, inputs, outputs, connections and clinical relevance
